newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble demand high after c.bank buying, T-bill sale.
newsitem.headline: Rouble demand high after c.bank buying, T-bill sale.

text.p: The rouble was steady on Thursday as funds were shifted to the government bond market and dealers said rouble supply was lower after commercial banks bought dollars actively from the central bank on Wednesday.

"There are more funds reserved in the T-bill trading system than usual (four trillion roubles). Besides banks are not buying dollars actively today (on the interbank market) so there is some rouble shortage," one dealer said.
She added overnight rouble credit rates could firm more today.
Aljba Alliance Bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said: "The day is quite hectic. There are some problems today getting roubles as they did not come in after (Wednesday's T-bill) auctions."
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,478-81 per dollar compared with an early 5,481-84 and 5,482-84 late on Wednesday. Tomorrow roubles were steady at 5,483-84 per dollar.
The central bank said it had set 5,476/5,486 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Thursday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 30-35 percent compared with Wednesday's late one to five percent.
